builder_plan.scenario: An assistant chooses the wrong API or sends arguments your product cannot use.
builder_plan.change: Apply the proposed tool-selection or argument-generation change in a sandbox.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current agent with the same tool schemas and task budget.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Correct completed actions, invalid calls, retries, latency, and cost per completed task.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Grounding LLM Agents in Business Processes: Process-Aware Knowledge Graphs for Reliable Multi-Step Service Invocation
summary: The technique replaces chunk-based retrieval-augmented service discovery that treats endpoints independently. It requires integrating OData metadata and BPMN processes into a typed property graph, increasing system complexity and retrieval latency. Potential failures include limited gains on services without process layers and residual invalid keys in write operations despite schema grounding.
rationale: The method directly improves reliability of LLM agents interacting with enterprise APIs by incorporating process and schema constraints, which is critical for production systems with limited infrastructure.
technique: Process-aware knowledge graph retrieval for LLM agents

claims.statement: The technique replaces chunk-based retrieval-augmented service discovery that treats endpoints independently. It requires integrating OData metadata and BPMN processes into a typed property graph, increasing system complexity and retrieval latency. Potential failures include limited gains on services without process layers and residual invalid keys in write operations despite schema grounding.

Improves Recall@3 by 5.7 points for queries with low lexical overlap; increases LLM agent task completion from 10.3% to 38.7% on multi-step queries; reduces invalid API calls to 3% with full typed context.
